q: A 64-year-old patient with severe COPD receiving oxygen at 4 L/min via nasal cannula becomes increasingly drowsy, confused, and difficult to rouse. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?
o: Increase oxygen flow to 6 L/min via simple face mask
Assess respiratory rate, depth, SpO2, and notify the physician for suspected CO2 narcosis
Place the patient flat in supine position
e: In chronic CO2 retainers (COPD), high-flow oxygen can blunt the hypoxic respiratory drive and worsen hypercapnia (CO2 narcosis). Immediately assess ventilation/SpO2 and titrate to target 88–92% while alerting the physician—never abruptly stop O2 or blindly increase flow.

q: A primigravida at 38 weeks gestation presents with BP 166/112 mmHg, severe frontal headache, blurred vision, epigastric pain, and 3+ patellar reflexes. What is the nurse's IMMEDIATE priority?
o: Encourage oral fluids and recheck BP after 1 hour
Notify the obstetrician immediately, initiate seizure precautions, and prepare IV Magnesium Sulfate
Place the mother in supine position and start oxytocin
Perform an immediate digital vaginal examination
e: BP >=160/110 with neurological symptoms, epigastric pain, and hyperreflexia indicates severe preeclampsia with imminent eclampsia. Immediate physician notification, left lateral positioning, seizure precautions, and MgSO4 prophylaxis are life-saving priorities.

q: On postoperative day 3 after total hip replacement, a patient suddenly develops sharp pleuritic chest pain, severe dyspnea, tachycardia (128 bpm), and SpO2 84%. What should the nurse do FIRST?
o: Ambulate the patient to relieve gas pain
Elevate the head of the bed (high-Fowler's), apply supplemental oxygen, and activate the rapid response team
Massage the patient's calves to check for tenderness
Administer oral aspirin and wait 30 minutes
e: Acute dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, and desaturation post-orthopedic surgery strongly indicate pulmonary embolism (PE). Elevating the head of bed and giving high-flow oxygen optimize gas exchange while rapid response/anticoagulation is mobilized. Never massage calves (risk of dislodging further thrombi).

q: During PPE removal (doffing) after caring for an isolation patient, which item should the nurse remove FIRST to minimize self-contamination?
e: CDC/AIIMS doffing sequence removes the most contaminated items first: Gloves -> Goggles/Face Shield -> Gown -> Mask/Respirator (followed by hand hygiene). Donning order is Gown -> Mask -> Goggles -> Gloves.

q: According to India's Biomedical Waste Management Rules, where should an IV tubing set and empty plastic saline bottle (without needle) be discarded?
e: Contaminated recyclable plastics (IV tubing, catheters, urine bags, syringes without fixed needles, gloves) go into the Red bag for autoclaving/shredding. Yellow is for anatomical/soiled waste; White is for sharps; Blue is for glassware/metallic implants.

q: When zeroing a Central Venous Pressure (CVP) transducer at the bedside, where must the nurse align the transducer's air-fluid interface?
o: 2nd intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line
4th intercostal space at the mid-axillary line (phlebostatic axis)
5th intercostal space at the left sternal border
e: The phlebostatic axis (4th intercostal space, mid-axillary line) approximates the level of the right atrium and is the mandatory zero-reference point for CVP and arterial line transducers. Normal CVP is 2–8 mmHg (3–12 cm H2O).

q: While recording a standard 12-lead ECG, where should precordial lead V1 be placed?
o: 4th intercostal space at the right sternal border
4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
5th intercostal space at the left mid-clavicular line
5th intercostal space at the left anterior axillary line
e: Precordial leads: V1 = 4th ICS right sternal border; V2 = 4th ICS left sternal border; V3 = midway between V2 and V4; V4 = 5th ICS left mid-clavicular line; V5 = anterior axillary line; V6 = mid-axillary line.

q: A mechanically ventilated ICU patient triggers a sudden HIGH-PRESSURE alarm. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?
o: Copious airway secretions, kinked tubing, or patient biting the ET tube
e: High-pressure alarms indicate increased airway resistance or decreased lung compliance (secretions needing suction, kinked/bitten ET tube, coughing, bronchospasm, pneumothorax). Low-pressure alarms indicate disconnection or cuff leak.

q: An ICU patient's arterial blood gas (ABG) shows: pH 7.26, PaCO2 58 mmHg, HCO3- 25 mEq/L. How should the nurse interpret this result?
e: pH < 7.35 (acidemia), PaCO2 > 45 mmHg (respiratory cause matching pH), and HCO3- is still normal (22–26 mEq/L), indicating uncompensated respiratory acidosis.

q: A patient in septic shock is receiving a peripheral IV infusion of Norepinephrine (Noradrenaline) and the nurse notices blanching, coolness, and swelling at the IV site. Which medication is infiltrated locally as the antidote for vasopressor extravasation?
e: Phentolamine (an alpha-adrenergic blocker) is injected subcutaneously around the extravasation site to reverse intense alpha-1 vasoconstriction and prevent tissue necrosis.

q: A patient on IV Heparin infusion for DVT has an aPTT of 115 seconds (control 30 seconds) and develops hematuria. What is the priority nursing action?
o: Stop the heparin infusion immediately, notify the physician, and prepare Protamine sulfate
Flush the IV line with normal saline and continue heparin
e: Therapeutic aPTT for heparin is typically 1.5–2.5× control (45–75 sec). Severe elevation with active bleeding requires immediate cessation of heparin and Protamine sulfate (specific antidote for heparin).

q: A woman receiving IV Magnesium Sulfate for severe preeclampsia has a respiratory rate of 10/min, urine output of 18 mL/hr, and absent deep tendon reflexes. Which antidote must the nurse administer as ordered?
e: Loss of patellar reflex is the earliest clinical sign of MgSO4 toxicity, followed by respiratory depression (<12/min) and oliguria (<30 mL/hr). Stop MgSO4 immediately and give 10% Calcium gluconate (10 mL IV slowly over 3–5 min).

q: A 4-year-old child arrives in the ER sitting upright leaning forward (tripod position), drooling saliva, with high fever (39.8°C) and muffled voice. Which nursing action is STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED?
o: Inspecting the child's throat with a tongue depressor
Keeping the child calm on the parent's lap
e: The 4 D's (Drooling, Dysphagia, Dysphonia, Distress) with tripod posture indicate acute epiglottitis. Never visualize the throat with a tongue blade or upset the child, as it can precipitate sudden complete laryngospasm and airway arrest.

q: A newborn assessed at 1 minute after birth has a pink body with blue extremities, heart rate 118 bpm, grimaces on suctioning, some flexion of extremities, and a weak irregular cry. What is the APGAR score?
e: Appearance (acrocyanosis) = 1, Pulse (>100) = 2, Grimace (grimace only) = 1, Activity (some flexion) = 1, Respiration (weak/irregular) = 1. Total = 6.

q: An agitated psychiatric patient begins pacing rapidly, clenching fists, and shouting threats in the dayroom. What is the nurse's FIRST intervention?
o: Maintain a safe distance, clear other patients, and use calm verbal de-escalation
Argue firmly to establish ward authority
Administer IV haloperidol without an order
e: Least-restrictive safety intervention comes first: ensure safety of others, maintain non-threatening posture and exit path, and use calm, clear verbal de-escalation before medications or restraints.

q: Ten minutes into a packed RBC transfusion, a patient develops chills, lower back pain, hypotension, and dark red urine. After stopping the transfusion IMMEDIATELY, what should the nurse do next?
o: Flush the existing blood tubing with normal saline
Disconnect the blood tubing at the hub and infuse 0.9% Normal Saline via NEW IV tubing
Administer acetaminophen and restart the transfusion slowly
Discard the blood bag in the red bin immediately
e: Suspected acute hemolytic transfusion reaction: NEVER flush the blood tubing (that pushes more incompatible blood into the patient). Attach new tubing with 0.9% NS to keep the vein open, notify the physician/blood bank, and return the blood bag + tubing to the blood bank.

q: A patient with Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) presents with blood glucose 580 mg/dL, pH 7.18, serum K+ 3.1 mEq/L, and severe dehydration. After initiating 0.9% Normal Saline, what must the nurse verify BEFORE starting IV Regular Insulin?
o: That serum sodium is below 120 mEq/L
That potassium replacement is initiated because insulin shifts K+ intracellularly and can trigger fatal hypokalemia
That oral glucose is given first
That IV bicarbonate is infused rapidly
e: Insulin drives potassium from extracellular fluid into cells. When serum K+ is <3.3 mEq/L in DKA, hold insulin and replace K+ first (once urine output is confirmed) to prevent lethal hypokalemic arrhythmias.

q: Under India's Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), what is the correct dose, route, and site for administering the BCG vaccine to a newborn at birth?
o: 0.5 mL intramuscular in the anterolateral thigh
0.05 mL intradermal in the left upper arm
0.1 mL subcutaneous in the right upper arm
e: BCG is given at birth (up to 1 month of age) as 0.05 mL intradermal in the left upper arm (deltoid insertion); after 1 month of age, the dose becomes 0.1 mL intradermal.

q: According to WHO Hand Hygiene guidelines, what is the recommended duration for alcohol-based hand rub versus washing hands with soap and water?
o: Hand rub 5–10 sec; soap & water 15–20 sec
Hand rub 20–30 sec; soap & water 40–60 sec
Hand rub 60 sec; soap & water 2 min
e: WHO specifies 20–30 seconds for alcohol-based hand rub (until dry) and 40–60 seconds for hand washing with soap and water (mandatory when hands are visibly soiled or after C. difficile care).

q: A cardiac monitor in the ICU suddenly displays chaotic, irregular, coarse undulations with no identifiable P waves or QRS complexes, and the patient is unresponsive with no pulse. What is the FIRST priority action?
o: Start high-quality CPR immediately and deliver unsynchronized defibrillation as soon as pads are attached
e: Pulseless Ventricular Fibrillation (V-Fib) is a shockable cardiac arrest rhythm. Immediate high-quality CPR and unsynchronized defibrillation (120–200 J biphasic) are the highest-priority survival interventions.

q: Which adverse effect is most characteristic of anticholinergic bronchodilators such as Ipratropium bromide?
e: Anticholinergics block muscarinic receptors ('Can't see, can't pee, can't spit, can't poop'), classically causing dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, and constipation.

q: Which cranial nerve is tested when the nurse asks a patient to shrug both shoulders against resistance and turn the head to each side?
e: CN XI (Spinal Accessory) innervates the sternocleidomastoid (head turning) and trapezius (shoulder shrug) muscles.

q: A nurse accidentally administers a double dose of an oral antihypertensive to a patient. After immediately assessing the patient's vitals and notifying the physician, how should the incident report be handled?
o: Staple the incident report inside the patient's medical chart
Complete an objective incident report separately for quality/risk management and document clinical findings in the patient's chart without mentioning the incident report
Delete the MAR entry to avoid liability
Wait until the next shift to report if BP stays normal
e: Incident reports are confidential internal risk-management documents—never place them in or reference them inside the patient's medical record. Always document objective patient assessments and provider notifications in the chart.

q: Which transmission-based precaution is required for a hospitalized patient with confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis (active smear-positive TB)?
o: Contact precautions with gown and gloves only
Airborne precautions in a negative-pressure isolation room (AIIR) with fit-tested N95 respirator
e: MTB ('MTV': Measles, Tuberculosis, Varicella) requires Airborne Precautions: negative-pressure room (>=12 ACH) with door closed and N95 respirator for staff.

q: In which year was the first All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS New Delhi) established by an Act of Parliament?
e: AIIMS New Delhi was established in 1956 as an Institution of National Importance under the AIIMS Act, 1956.

q: Which national initiative in India specifically aims to improve the quality of care in labor rooms and maternity operation theaters in public health facilities?
e: LaQshya (Labour Room Quality Improvement Initiative) targets intrapartum and immediate postpartum care quality in public labor rooms and maternity OTs.

q: A physician orders 500 mL of Normal Saline to infuse over 4 hours using a tubing set with a drop factor of 20 gtt/mL. What is the drip rate (rounded to nearest whole number)?
Find the next number in the series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
Which immunoglobulin is the ONLY class that normally crosses the human placenta to provide passive immunity to the newborn?
e: IgG crosses the placenta (natural passive immunity). IgA is abundant in breast milk/colostrum; IgM is the first antibody in acute infection; IgE mediates type I hypersensitivity.

q: International Nurses Day is celebrated worldwide every year on May 12 to commemorate the birth anniversary of:
e: International Nurses Day (May 12) honors Florence Nightingale (born May 12, 1820), founder of modern nursing.

q: Six hours after a subtotal thyroidectomy, a patient reports tingling around the lips and fingertips and develops inspiratory stridor. Which TWO items are the most critical bedside emergency supplies?
o: Chest tube tray and normal saline
Emergency tracheostomy set and IV 10% Calcium gluconate
e: Post-thyroidectomy emergencies include neck hematoma/laryngeal edema causing stridor (tracheostomy set) and hypoparathyroidism causing acute hypocalcemic tetany/laryngospasm (IV Calcium gluconate).

q: A patient taking Lithium carbonate for bipolar disorder starts a low-sodium diet and develops coarse hand tremors, vomiting, and slurred speech. Why did toxicity occur?
o: Low sodium increases renal lithium excretion
Sodium depletion causes increased renal reabsorption of lithium in the proximal tubule
Low sodium converts lithium into toxic metabolites
e: The kidneys handle lithium similarly to sodium; low sodium intake or dehydration causes the proximal tubule to reabsorb more lithium, rapidly pushing serum lithium >1.5 mEq/L into toxicity.

q: A patient taking Digoxin and Furosemide reports nausea, blurred yellow-green vision halos, and has an apical pulse of 52 bpm. Which lab abnormality most strongly predisposes to this toxicity?
e: Loop diuretics like Furosemide deplete potassium; hypokalemia increases digoxin binding to Na+/K+-ATPase, precipitating digitalis toxicity (bradycardia, GI upset, xanthopsia/yellow-green halos).

q: Before dispensing the weekly supply of Clozapine to a patient with treatment-resistant schizophrenia, which mandatory laboratory parameter must the nurse review?
e: Clozapine carries a severe risk of agranulocytosis; regular CBC/ANC monitoring is mandatory, and the drug must be held immediately if fever, sore throat, or low ANC develops.

q: During an antenatal abdominal examination, the nurse grasps the lower uterine segment just above the symphysis pubis between thumb and fingers to determine presentation and engagement. Which Leopold's maneuver is this?
e: Third Leopold's maneuver (Pawlik's grip) grasps the lower pole above the symphysis pubis to identify the presenting part and whether it is engaged (mobile vs fixed).

q: A pregnant woman at 34 weeks arrives with painless, bright-red vaginal bleeding. Vital signs are stable and FHR is 144 bpm. Which nursing intervention is STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED?
o: Preparing for bedside ultrasound localization of the placenta
e: Painless bright-red third-trimester bleeding is classic for Placenta Previa. A digital vaginal exam can tear placental vessels and trigger catastrophic maternal-fetal hemorrhage.

q: Immediately after vaginal delivery of the placenta, a woman develops heavy vaginal bleeding and a soft, boggy uterus displaced to the right of the umbilicus. What is the nurse's FIRST action?
o: Pack the vagina tightly with dry gauze
Perform firm fundal massage and assess/empty the urinary bladder while administering ordered uterotonics
Place the woman in Trendelenburg and wait 20 minutes
Apply an ice pack to the perineum
e: Uterine atony is the #1 cause of PPH; a boggy uterus deviated to the right signals a distended bladder preventing uterine contraction. Firm fundal massage + bladder emptying + uterotonics (Oxytocin first-line) are immediate priorities.

q: Immediately after spontaneous rupture of membranes, the nurse sees a pulsating loop of umbilical cord protruding from the vagina and FHR drops to 78 bpm. What is the IMMEDIATE nursing action?
o: Attempt to push the cord back inside the uterus
Insert a sterile gloved hand to lift the fetal presenting part off the cord and place the mother in knee-chest/Trendelenburg position
Increase the oxytocin drip to speed up delivery
Turn the mother supine and monitor for 5 minutes
e: Umbilical cord prolapse causes fatal fetal hypoxia via cord compression. Keep sterile gloved fingers pushing the presenting part upward off the cord until emergency C-section, stop oxytocin, give O2, and cover exposed cord with warm sterile saline gauze.

q: Which Bishop score generally indicates a favorable (ripe) cervix with a high likelihood of successful vaginal induction of labor?
e: Bishop score (0–13) evaluates dilation, effacement, station, cervical consistency, and position. A score >=8 predicts successful induction similar to spontaneous labor.

q: Using the Holliday-Segar (4-2-1 / 100-50-20) formula, what is the 24-hour maintenance IV fluid requirement for a child weighing 18 kg?
e: Holliday-Segar: First 10 kg × 100 mL = 1,000 mL; Next 8 kg × 50 mL = 400 mL. Total = 1,400 mL/24 hours.

q: An adult weighing 70 kg sustains deep partial-thickness burns over 40% TBSA at 08:00 AM. Using the Parkland formula (4 mL × kg × %TBSA), how much Ringer's Lactate should be infused in the FIRST 8 hours from the time of burn?
e: Total 24-hr fluid = 4 × 70 × 40 = 11,200 mL. Half (5,600 mL) is given in the first 8 hours from the time of burn injury, and the remaining 5,600 mL over the next 16 hours.

q: A patient with a right-sided chest tube (ICD) for pneumothorax has continuous vigorous bubbling in the water-seal chamber. What does this finding indicate?
o: An air leak in the drainage system or chest tube insertion site
e: In a water-seal chamber, gentle tidaling (fluctuation with breathing) and intermittent bubbling during coughing are expected; continuous bubbling signifies an air leak (inspect connections/dressing—never clamp routinely).

q: When performing open endotracheal or tracheostomy suctioning in an adult, what is the safe maximum suction duration per pass and recommended vacuum pressure?
o: 10–15 seconds at 80–120 mmHg (apply suction ONLY while withdrawing)
e: Pre-oxygenate with 100% O2, insert catheter without suction until resistance, then apply intermittent suction at 80–120 mmHg for no longer than 10–15 seconds while rotating and withdrawing to prevent hypoxia and mucosal trauma.

q: After performing a Mantoux (tuberculin skin) test, when and how should the nurse interpret the result?
o: After 48–72 hours by measuring the transverse diameter of induration (hardness) in millimeters
After 7 days by checking for blistering
e: Mantoux (PPD) is read at 48–72 hours by palpating and measuring induration (NOT erythema) in mm. >=5 mm positive in HIV/immunosuppressed; >=10 mm in healthcare workers/high-risk; >=15 mm in general low-risk population.

q: Before drawing an arterial blood gas (ABG) sample from the radial artery, the nurse performs a modified Allen's test. A normal (positive) test confirms:
o: Adequate collateral circulation to the hand via the ulnar artery (palm flushes pink within 5–15 seconds)
e: Compressing both radial and ulnar arteries blanches the palm; releasing the ulnar artery should restore pink flush within 5–15 seconds, proving safe collateral flow if radial thrombosis occurs.

q: A head-injury patient opens eyes only to painful stimulus, utters inappropriate words, and withdraws limbs from pain. What is this patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score?
e: Eye opening to pain (E2) + Inappropriate words (V3) + Normal withdrawal from pain (M4) = 9. Remember GCS <=8 indicates coma/need for airway protection ('8, intubate').

q: Which biomedical waste container is used to dispose of broken glass ampoules, empty glass medicine vials, and metallic body implants?
e: Glassware (broken/discarded vials, ampoules, slides) and metallic body implants go into the Blue box; needles, blades, and scalpels go into the White sharps container.

q: Which developmental milestone red flag in a 9-month-old infant warrants immediate pediatric referral?
o: Unable to sit without support and does not babble
e: A healthy infant sits unsupported by 7–8 months and babbles by 6–9 months (stranger anxiety is normal at 8–9 months). Walking independently occurs around 12–15 months.

q: In a patient with postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony who ALSO has severe hypertension (BP 170/106 mmHg), which uterotonic drug is CONTRAINDICATED?
e: Methylergometrine (ergot alkaloid) causes potent systemic vasoconstriction and is strictly contraindicated in hypertension, preeclampsia, and cardiac disease. Carboprost (PGF2-alpha) is contraindicated in bronchial asthma.

q: Immediately after a lumbar puncture (spinal tap) or spinal anesthesia, which position and measure best help prevent post-dural puncture headache?
o: Flat/supine position for several hours with liberal oral or IV hydration
Trendelenburg position with head hanging down
e: Keeping the patient flat/recumbent and well hydrated minimizes CSF leakage through the dural puncture site and reduces spinal headache.

q: Following a right modified radical mastectomy, how should the nurse manage the patient's right arm?
o: Take blood pressures and draw blood from the right arm only
Elevate the right arm on a pillow and post a sign prohibiting BP readings, venipuncture, or IV lines on the right arm
Keep the right arm tightly dependent below heart level
Apply hot compresses continuously to the axilla
e: Axillary lymph node dissection impairs lymphatic drainage; elevating the affected arm and strictly avoiding BP cuffs, IVs, and needle sticks prevent lymphedema and cellulitis.

q: A patient newly diagnosed with terminal cancer insists, 'The lab must have mixed up my biopsy slides—I feel completely healthy.' Which defense mechanism is the patient using?
e: Denial is the unconscious refusal to accept a painful reality or diagnosis—common as an initial coping stage in grief (Kubler-Ross).

q: In epidemiology, the denominator used to calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is:
e: MMR = (Maternal deaths during a given period / Total live births in the same period) × 100,000. Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) uses 1,000 live births.

q: A patient prescribed Isoniazid (INH) for pulmonary tuberculosis should receive which vitamin supplement to prevent peripheral neuropathy?
e: Isoniazid interferes with pyridoxine metabolism, causing sensory peripheral neuropathy; prophylactic Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) prevents this complication.

q: Which anatomical structure prevents aspiration of food or liquids into the trachea during swallowing?
e: During deglutition, the larynx elevates and the leaf-shaped elastic cartilage epiglottis folds backward over the glottis to seal the airway.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) located?
e: WHO was founded on April 7, 1948 (celebrated as World Health Day) with its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: A vial of Amikacin contains 500 mg in 2 mL. The doctor orders 350 mg IM. How many milliliters should the nurse draw up?
e: Volume = (Desired / Have) × Quantity = (350 / 500) × 2 mL = 0.7 × 2 = 1.4 mL.

q: Pointing to a photograph, Maya says, 'He is the only son of my grandfather's only son.' How is the man in the photograph related to Maya?
e: Maya's grandfather's only son is Maya's father; his only son is Maya's brother.

q: Which clotting factor is deficient in classic Hemophilia A?
e: Hemophilia A = Factor VIII deficiency (X-linked recessive); Hemophilia B (Christmas disease) = Factor IX deficiency.

q: The 'Kayakalp' award scheme launched by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare evaluates public health facilities primarily on:
o: Cleanliness, hygiene, waste management, and infection control practices
e: Kayakalp (launched 2015 under Swachh Bharat Abhiyan) incentivizes public hospitals and AIIMS/DH/PHCs for high standards of sanitation, BMW management, and infection control.

q: A patient with a T4 spinal cord injury develops hypotension (BP 76/44 mmHg), bradycardia (HR 46 bpm), and warm, dry skin. Which type of shock is present?
e: Neurogenic shock (loss of sympathetic tone in injuries at or above T6) uniquely causes hypotension WITH bradycardia and warm dry skin—unlike hypovolemic/cardiogenic shock which cause tachycardia and cool clammy skin.

q: A traumatic brain injury patient's BP rises from 124/76 to 176/68 mmHg, heart rate drops from 84 to 50 bpm, and respirations become irregular. What does this classic triad signify?
o: Cushing's triad indicating critically increased ICP and impending brainstem herniation
e: Cushing's triad = Widening pulse pressure (systolic hypertension), bradycardia, and irregular respirations—a late emergency sign of severe increased ICP.

q: Which medication is the first-line emergency IV drug to terminate active status epilepticus?
o: IV Lorazepam (or IV Diazepam / IM Midazolam)
e: Fast-acting benzodiazepines—specifically IV Lorazepam (0.1 mg/kg, max 4 mg)—are first-line for rapidly stopping status epilepticus, followed by a loading dose of fosphenytoin, levetiracetam, or valproate.

q: A patient arrives in the ER with acute right-sided hemiplegia and aphasia that started 90 minutes ago. Before IV Alteplase (tPA) thrombolysis can be given, what is the FIRST diagnostic test required?
o: Non-contrast CT scan of the head to rule out intracranial hemorrhage
e: Non-contrast head CT is mandatory immediately (target door-to-CT <25 min) to exclude hemorrhagic stroke before administering IV tPA within the 4.5-hour window.

q: A CKD patient has a serum potassium of 6.9 mEq/L and ECG shows tall peaked T waves and widened QRS complexes. Which IV medication protects the myocardium IMMEDIATELY (within 1–3 minutes)?
e: IV Calcium gluconate immediately stabilizes the cardiac cell membrane against lethal V-Fib/asystole (does not lower serum K+ itself). IV Regular Insulin + 50% Dextrose and nebulized Salbutamol then shift K+ intracellularly.

q: After pituitary surgery (transsphenoidal hypophysectomy), a patient excretes 450 mL/hr of pale, dilute urine with specific gravity 1.002 and serum Na+ 154 mEq/L. Which complication has developed?
e: ADH deficiency after pituitary surgery causes massive polyuria, low urine specific gravity (<1.005), and hypernatremia (Diabetes Insipidus), treated with IV fluids and Desmopressin (DDAVP).

q: While a nurse is removing a subclavian Central Venous Catheter (CVC), the patient gasps and suddenly becomes dyspneic, cyanotic, and hypotensive with a 'mill-wheel' heart murmur. What is the IMMEDIATE positioning action?
o: Left lateral Trendelenburg position (Durant's maneuver), administer 100% O2, and notify the physician
e: Suspected venous air embolism: Durant's maneuver (left lateral decubitus with head down/Trendelenburg) traps air in the right atrium apex, preventing it from blocking the pulmonary artery outflow tract.

q: In standard ISO color-coding of peripheral IV cannulas, which gauge corresponds to GREEN and PINK cannulas respectively?
e: Standard IV cannula colors: 14G Orange, 16G Grey, 18G Green (~90 mL/min, ideal for blood transfusion/trauma), 20G Pink (~60 mL/min, routine adult IV), 22G Blue, 24G Yellow, 26G Violet.

q: Which postoperative position is safest immediately following a pediatric tonsillectomy while the child is still drowsy from anesthesia?
o: Side-lying (lateral) or prone with head turned to the side
e: Side-lying/prone position facilitates drainage of secretions/blood out of the mouth and prevents aspiration. Frequent swallowing is an early sign of post-tonsillectomy hemorrhage!

q: After posterior-approach total hip arthroplasty, which movement must the nurse instruct the patient to STRICTLY AVOID to prevent hip dislocation?
o: Using an abduction pillow between the legs
Flexing the hip beyond 90 degrees, crossing the legs (adduction), or internal rotation
e: Posterior hip precautions prevent dislocation: never flex hip >90°, never cross legs/adduct past midline, and never internally rotate the operated leg; keep an abduction pillow in place.

q: A patient with liver cirrhosis and hepatic encephalopathy is prescribed oral Lactulose. Which clinical outcome confirms the drug is working effectively?
o: 2–3 soft stools per day, improved mental alertness, and declining serum ammonia
Weight gain of 3 kg in 2 days
e: Lactulose traps ammonia (NH3 -> NH4+) in the acidic colon lumen and expels it via stool; titrate dose to produce 2–3 soft bowel movements daily and improved orientation.

q: In acute pancreatitis, bluish discoloration around the umbilicus and over the flanks are named respectively:
o: Cullen's sign and Grey Turner's sign
e: Cullen's sign (periumbilical ecchymosis) and Grey Turner's sign (flank ecchymosis) indicate retroperitoneal hemorrhage in severe necrotizing acute pancreatitis.

q: An arterial blood gas reveals: pH 7.51, PaCO2 42 mmHg, HCO3- 34 mEq/L in a patient with 3 days of continuous nasogastric suctioning. What is the acid-base imbalance?
e: Prolonged vomiting or NG suctioning loses gastric HCl, elevating HCO3- (>26) and pH (>7.45) with normal PaCO2 (35–45) = uncompensated metabolic alkalosis.

q: During an adult cardiac arrest code, what is the standard IV/IO dose and repeat interval of Epinephrine (Adrenaline 1:10,000)?
e: AHA ACLS guidelines specify Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO (10 mL of 1:10,000) every 3–5 minutes during cardiac arrest, followed by a 20 mL saline flush.

q: Which first-line IV antiarrhythmic is recommended in ACLS for shock-refractory Ventricular Fibrillation or pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia?
o: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO bolus (followed by 150 mg if needed)
e: Amiodarone (300 mg first bolus, 150 mg second dose) or Lidocaine is used for refractory VF/pVT. Adenosine is used for stable narrow-complex SVT.

q: A patient with symptomatic sinus bradycardia (HR 38 bpm, BP 80/50 mmHg, dizzy) requires immediate emergency drug therapy per ACLS guidelines. Which drug is first-line?
o: IV Atropine 1 mg bolus (every 3–5 min, max 3 mg)
e: Updated AHA ACLS guidelines specify Atropine 1 mg IV bolus every 3–5 minutes (maximum 3 mg) as first-line treatment for symptomatic bradycardia; if ineffective, start transcutaneous pacing or Dopamine/Epinephrine infusion.

q: When placing a patient for a thoracentesis to drain a right pleural effusion, which position is optimal?
o: Sitting upright on the edge of the bed leaning forward over an overbed pillow/table
e: Sitting upright leaning forward widens intercostal spaces and drops the diaphragm downward; instruct the patient not to cough or move during needle insertion.

q: Which isolation precaution is mandatory for a patient diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infectious diarrhea?
o: Contact precautions (gown + gloves) and hand washing with SOAP AND WATER (not alcohol gel)
e: C. difficile forms hardy spores that alcohol-based hand rubs do NOT kill; mandatory soap-and-water handwashing and bleach/sporicidal disinfection are required alongside Contact precautions.

q: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks presents with sudden severe abdominal pain, a board-like rigid tender uterus, dark-red vaginal bleeding, and fetal distress. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Abruptio placentae (premature separation of normally implanted placenta)
e: Painful dark bleeding + rigid ('woody') tender uterus + fetal distress/coagulopathy = Abruptio placentae. Placenta previa is painless bright-red bleeding with a soft non-tender uterus.

q: Which assessment sign helps differentiate true bacterial Meningitis from simple febrile illness in an older child?
o: Nuchal rigidity with positive Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs
e: Meningeal irritation produces neck stiffness, Kernig's sign (pain/resistance extending flexed knee), and Brudzinski's sign (involuntary hip/knee flexion when neck is passively flexed).

q: Which level of prevention is represented by Pap smear screening for early detection of cervical cancer?
e: Screening and early diagnosis/prompt treatment (Pap smear, mammography, BP screening) = Secondary prevention. Immunization/health promotion = Primary; rehabilitation = Tertiary.

q: A client with depression suddenly tells the nurse, 'You won't have to worry about me anymore; I gave away my watch and feel totally at peace.' How should the nurse interpret this?
o: The patient is completely cured and ready for discharge
A high-risk warning sign of imminent suicidal intent requiring immediate safety assessment and 1:1 observation
e: Giving away prized possessions, sudden calm/relief after severe depression, and cryptic farewell statements are classic red flags of a finalized suicide plan.

q: Where does the spinal cord normally terminate (conus medullaris) in an adult, making L3–L4 or L4–L5 safe for lumbar puncture?
e: In adults, the spinal cord ends at L1–L2 (in neonates, around L3), so inserting a lumbar puncture needle at L3–L4 or L4–L5 enters the subarachnoid cauda equina space safely.

q: In nursing management, 'Span of Control' refers to:
o: The total budget controlled by a nursing superintendent
The number of subordinates who can be effectively supervised directly by one manager
The length of a nurse's shift
The geographic distance between hospital wards
e: Span of control defines how many direct reports one supervisor can effectively oversee without losing quality or safety.

q: When inserting a nasogastric (Ryle's) tube in an adult, how does the nurse measure the proper insertion length (NEX measurement)?
o: Tip of the nose to earlobe to xiphoid process
e: NEX (Nose -> Earlobe -> Xiphoid process) estimates insertion length; confirm placement via X-ray (gold standard) or gastric aspirate pH (<=5.5) before feeding.

q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act lowered the voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years?
e: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act (1988, effective 1989) amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18.

q: If 12 nurses can complete a ward vaccination audit in 10 days, how many days will 15 nurses take working at the same rate?
e: Inverse proportion: 12 × 10 = 15 × D -> D = 120 / 15 = 8 days.

q: Choose the odd one out:
e: Stethoscope, sphygmomanometer, and thermometer are diagnostic/vital-sign instruments; an ampoule is a medication container.

q: Which hormone secreted by the posterior pituitary regulates water reabsorption in the renal collecting ducts?
e: ADH (synthesized in the hypothalamus, stored/released by posterior pituitary) inserts aquaporin-2 channels in collecting ducts to conserve water.

q: The National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) uses which digital portal for real-time TB patient tracking and Direct Benefit Transfer (Nikshay Poshan Yojana)?
e: Ni-kshay is India's national TB surveillance & DBT portal; U-WIN digitizes Universal Immunization Programme vaccination records.

q: On a continuous fetal heart rate tracing (CTG), gradual decelerations that begin AFTER the peak of a uterine contraction and recover after the contraction ends (Late Decelerations) indicate:
e: VEAL CHOP: Late decelerations = Placental insufficiency. Priority nursing steps: Turn mother to left lateral side, stop oxytocin, give IV fluid bolus, administer O2 (8–10 L/min), and notify obstetrician.

q: During vaginal delivery, the fetal head delivers and retracts tightly against the perineum ('turtle sign'), indicating shoulder dystocia. What is the FIRST maneuver the nurse should assist with?
o: McRoberts maneuver (hyperflexing maternal thighs onto abdomen) with suprapubic pressure
Pulling forcefully on the fetal head
e: McRoberts maneuver + suprapubic pressure resolves most shoulder dystocias by straightening the sacrum and dislodging the anterior shoulder. Fundal pressure is strictly contraindicated (risks uterine rupture/brachial plexus injury).

q: On a WHO modified partograph, cervical dilation plotting begins on the Alert Line at what dilation, and what does crossing the Action Line signify?
o: 4 cm; need for urgent obstetric reassessment/intervention for prolonged or obstructed labor
e: The modified partograph starts at active labor (4 cm dilation, expected >=1 cm/hr); the Action line is 4 hours right of the Alert line and signals need for active intervention.

q: An Rh-negative mother delivers an Rh-positive baby. Within what timeframe must Rho(D) immune globulin (Anti-D 300 mcg IM) be administered to prevent future isoimmunization?
o: Only during the next pregnancy at 36 weeks
e: Anti-D (300 mcg IM) is given routinely at 28 weeks gestation and within 72 hours postpartum if the newborn is Rh-positive (and Indirect Coombs test is negative).

q: While caring for a jaundiced neonate under blue-light phototherapy, which nursing intervention is ESSENTIAL?
o: Apply oil/lotion generously to the infant's skin
Shield the newborn's eyes and genitalia, reposition frequently, and monitor hydration/temperature
Keep the baby fully clothed to prevent chilling
e: Protect retinas with opaque eye shields (remove during feeding to assess eyes/bonding), expose maximal skin (diaper only), avoid oils (cause thermal burns), and maintain frequent breastfeeding/hydration.

q: Which chest X-ray classic silhouette corresponds to Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection (TAPVC) respectively?
o: Boot-shaped heart (coeur en sabot) and Snowman / Figure-of-8 sign
e: TOF -> Boot-shaped heart; TAPVC -> Snowman (figure-of-8) sign; Transposition of Great Arteries (TGA) -> Egg-on-a-string; Pericardial effusion -> Water-bottle heart.

q: Which medication is administered to medically close a hemodynamically significant Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) in a preterm newborn?
e: NSAIDs (Indomethacin/Ibuprofen) inhibit prostaglandins to close a PDA, whereas Prostaglandin E1 (Alprostadil) is given to KEEP the ductus open in duct-dependent lesions like TGA or severe TOF.

q: What are the three core components of Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for stable low-birth-weight (<2000 g) newborns?
o: Incubator warming, formula feeding, and prolonged hospital stay
Continuous skin-to-skin contact, exclusive breastfeeding, and early discharge with follow-up
Radiant warmer, IV dextrose, and phototherapy
Swaddling in wool blankets, bottle feeding, and antibiotics
e: KMC stabilizes newborn temperature, heart/respiratory rate, promotes exclusive breastfeeding, reduces neonatal sepsis, and strengthens maternal-infant bonding.

q: A preterm infant born to a mother with gestational diabetes develops jitteriness, weak cry, and blood glucose of 32 mg/dL. What is the immediate nursing priority if symptomatic?
o: Administer ordered IV 10% Dextrose bolus (2 mL/kg) followed by continuous dextrose infusion and frequent glucose monitoring
e: Infants of diabetic mothers have hyperinsulinemia and are at high risk for severe hypoglycemia (<40–45 mg/dL). Symptomatic hypoglycemia requires immediate IV 10% Dextrose (2 mL/kg) to prevent permanent neurological injury.

q: A patient taking Haloperidol develops high fever (40.2°C), severe 'lead-pipe' muscular rigidity, autonomic instability, and markedly elevated serum Creatine Kinase (CK). Which emergency condition is this?
e: NMS is a life-threatening antipsychotic reaction (Fever + Encephalopathy + Vitals instability + Elevated CK + Rigidity — 'FEVER'). Stop the antipsychotic immediately, cool the patient, hydrate, and prepare Dantrolene or Bromocriptine.

q: A patient started on a first-generation antipsychotic suddenly develops upward rolling of the eyes (oculogyric crisis) and painful neck twisting (torticollis). Which emergency medication reverses this acute dystonia?
e: Acute extrapyramidal dystonia responds rapidly to parenteral anticholinergics (Benztropine or Diphenhydramine).

q: Which dietary teaching is critical for a patient prescribed Tranylcypromine or Phenelzine (MAOIs)?
o: Avoid tyramine-rich aged/fermented foods (aged cheese, cured meats, soy sauce, red wine) to prevent hypertensive crisis
Consume high-tyramine foods to boost efficacy
e: Tyramine triggers massive norepinephrine release when MAO is inhibited, causing life-threatening hypertensive crisis (severe occipital headache, BP spike).

q: Before modified Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT), which two drug classes are routinely given to prevent fractures and reduce secretions/bradycardia?
e: Modified ECT uses an anticholinergic (atropine/glycopyrrolate), ultra-short anesthetic (methohexital/propofol), and neuromuscular blocker (succinylcholine) under 100% oxygenation.

q: A patient with cirrhosis develops massive hematemesis from ruptured esophageal varices and a Sengstaken-Blakemore tube is inserted. Which emergency tool MUST be kept taped at the bedside?
o: A pair of sharp scissors (to immediately cut and deflate balloons if airway obstruction occurs)
e: If the gastric balloon migrates upward and occludes the airway, the nurse must immediately cut all lumens with bedside scissors and remove the tube.

q: In a patient with an arteriovenous (AV) fistula in the left forearm for hemodialysis, how does the nurse verify fistula patency each shift?
o: Take blood pressure on the left arm
Palpate for a vibration ('thrill') and auscultate for a swooshing sound ('bruit')
Check radial pulse only on the right arm
Apply a tight elastic bandage over the fistula
e: A patent AV fistula always has a palpable thrill and audible bruit; sudden absence signals thrombosis—notify the physician immediately. Never perform BP, IVs, or labs on the fistula arm.

q: In nursing research, a sampling technique where every member of the target population has an equal, known non-zero chance of being selected is called:
e: Probability sampling (simple random, stratified, systematic, cluster) minimizes selection bias and allows statistical generalization.

q: Which vaccine is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy because it is a live attenuated vaccine?
e: Live attenuated vaccines (MMR, Varicella, BCG, Yellow Fever) are contraindicated during pregnancy due to theoretical fetal risk; Td and inactivated flu vaccines are safe and recommended.

q: Which pressure injury stage is characterized by full-thickness skin loss with visible subcutaneous fat, possible slough, but NO exposed bone, tendon, or muscle?
e: Stage 1: non-blanchable intact skin; Stage 2: partial-thickness dermis loss/blister; Stage 3: full-thickness into subcutaneous fat; Stage 4: exposed bone, tendon, or muscle.

q: A patient receiving IV Vancomycin develops sudden flushing of the face, neck, and upper chest with pruritus (Red Man Syndrome). What is the appropriate nursing action?
o: Increase the infusion speed to finish sooner
Slow/pause the infusion, notify the physician, give ordered antihistamine, and infuse future doses over at least 60–90 minutes
Label the patient as permanently allergic to all antibiotics
Administer IV epinephrine for every mild flush
e: Red Man Syndrome is a rate-related non-IgE mast cell histamine release, prevented by infusing Vancomycin slowly (>=60–90 min).

q: What is the standard diagnostic screening test used in India (DIPSI guidelines) for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)?
o: Single-step 75 g oral glucose test with 2-hour plasma glucose >= 140 mg/dL (regardless of last meal)
e: Under India's DIPSI/MoHFW guidelines, a single-step 75 g oral glucose load with 2-hour plasma glucose >=140 mg/dL diagnoses GDM.

q: Which layer of the meninges is the innermost, delicate vascular membrane tightly adherent to the surface of the brain and spinal cord?
e: From outside to inside ('DAP'): Dura mater (tough outer), Arachnoid mater (web-like middle; subarachnoid space holds CSF), Pia mater (innermost adherent layer).

q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
e: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states (~1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

q: A medicine bottle costs ₹480 after a 20% discount. What was its original marked price?
e: 80% of Marked Price = 480 -> Marked Price = 480 / 0.80 = ₹600.

q: If HOSPITAL is coded as IPTQJUBM, how is DOCTOR coded?
e: Each letter shifts +1 forward: D->E, O->P, C->D, T->U, O->P, R->S = EPDUPS.

q: The 'SUMAN' (Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan) initiative guarantees pregnant women and sick newborns:
o: Assured, dignified, respectful, and zero-expense quality maternal and newborn care at public health facilities
e: SUMAN aims for zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths with zero-expense delivery, C-section, referral transport, and respectful care at public facilities.

q: According to Spaulding's classification, a flexible fiberoptic bronchoscope or GI endoscope that contacts intact mucous membranes requires at minimum:
o: High-level disinfection (e.g., 2% Glutaraldehyde / OPA) or sterilization
e: Spaulding classification: Critical items (enter sterile tissue/vascular system -> Sterilization); Semi-critical (mucous membranes, e.g., endoscopes, laryngoscope blades -> High-level disinfection); Non-critical (intact skin, e.g., BP cuff -> Low-level disinfection).

q: What is the maximum safe time allowed to complete the infusion of a single unit of Packed Red Blood Cells (PRBC) once removed from the blood bank refrigerator?
e: Start transfusion within 30 minutes of issue and complete within 4 hours to prevent bacterial proliferation; infuse via a 170–260 micron standard blood filter with 0.9% NS only.

q: When drawing up Regular (short-acting, clear) and NPH (intermediate-acting, cloudy) insulin into the SAME syringe, which sequence is correct?
o: Draw up NPH (cloudy) first, then Regular (clear)
Inject air into NPH -> inject air into Regular -> draw up Regular (clear) first -> draw up NPH (cloudy) second
Mix both vials vigorously before drawing
Glargine can be freely mixed with Regular insulin
e: Remember 'RN' (Regular before NPH / Clear before Cloudy) so cloudy protamine doesn't contaminate the clear Regular vial. NEVER mix Insulin Glargine or Detemir with any other insulin.

q: On a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM), when must a vaccine vial be DISCARDED and NOT used?
o: Stage 1 (inner square lighter than outer circle)
Stage 2 (inner square slightly darker than Stage 1 but still lighter than outer circle)
Stage 3 or Stage 4 (inner square matches or is darker than the outer circle)
Whenever the vial has been taken out of the fridge for 5 minutes
e: VVM Discard Point: once the inner square becomes the SAME color as (Stage 3) or DARKER than (Stage 4) the outer reference ring, cumulative heat exposure has ruined potency—discard immediately.

q: In a Primary Health Centre (PHC), which vaccine is stored at the BOTTOM of the Ice-Lined Refrigerator (ILR) because it is most heat-sensitive and freeze-tolerant?
e: The bottom of an ILR is coldest: store freeze-tolerant/heat-sensitive OPV & Measles/MR at the bottom, and freeze-sensitive 'T-series' vaccines (Td, Pentavalent, HepB, IPV) in the upper baskets (ILR temp +2°C to +8°C).

q: Match the correct specific antidote for Opioid overdose and Benzodiazepine overdose respectively:
e: Naloxone reverses opioid respiratory depression; Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepine sedation; N-acetylcysteine reverses paracetamol; Deferoxamine chelates iron overdose.

q: A patient with mechanical mitral valve replacement is taking oral Warfarin. Which lab test and typical target therapeutic range monitor safety and efficacy?
e: Warfarin is monitored via PT/INR (2.0–3.0 for DVT/PE/AFib; 2.5–3.5 for mechanical mitral valves). Antidote is Vitamin K (phytonadione) and FFP/PCC for life-threatening bleeding.

q: Which laboratory indicator is the MOST specific and gold-standard biomarker for diagnosing Acute Myocardial Infarction?
e: Cardiac Troponin I and T rise within 3–6 hours of myocardial necrosis, peak at 12–24 hours, and remain elevated for 7–14 days with highest myocardial specificity.

q: What is the normal composition of blood vessels inside a healthy human umbilical cord?
o: 2 arteries (carrying deoxygenated blood from fetus) and 1 vein (carrying oxygenated blood to fetus)
e: Remember 'AVA': 2 Umbilical Arteries (deoxygenated blood from fetus to placenta) and 1 Umbilical Vein (oxygenated nutrient-rich blood from placenta to fetus).

q: In a child with severe dehydration due to acute watery diarrhea (Plan C under IMNCI), what is the preferred IV fluid for rapid resuscitation?
o: Ringer's Lactate (100 mL/kg divided per age protocol)
e: WHO/IMNCI Plan C uses Ringer's Lactate (100 mL/kg): for infants <12 mo -> 30 mL/kg in 1 hr + 70 mL/kg in 5 hrs; for children >=12 mo -> 30 mL/kg in 30 min + 70 mL/kg in 2.5 hrs.

q: A patient believes firmly that news anchors on television are sending secret personal messages specifically to him. This fixed false belief is called:
e: Delusion of reference attributes personal meaning/messages to neutral public events, broadcasts, or gestures.

q: Which part of the brain regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst, circadian rhythm, and pituitary hormone release?
e: The hypothalamus is the master homeostatic thermostat and neuroendocrine regulator linking the nervous and endocrine systems.

q: What are the standard parameters for gravity-displacement steam sterilization in a hospital autoclave?
e: Autoclaving at 121°C (250°F), 15 psi for 15–20 minutes destroys vegetative bacteria, viruses, and resistant bacterial spores (tested biologically with Geobacillus stearothermophilus).

q: During peritoneal dialysis, the nurse observes that the drained dialysate effluent is cloudy and opaque, and the patient has abdominal tenderness. What does this indicate?
o: Peritonitis (most serious complication of peritoneal dialysis)
e: Cloudy peritoneal dialysate effluent is the earliest hallmark of peritonitis; send effluent for cell count/culture and initiate ordered intraperitoneal antibiotics promptly.

q: Under Ayushman Bharat — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), what is the annual health insurance coverage per eligible family for secondary and tertiary hospitalization?
e: PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh per family per year for cashless secondary and tertiary hospitalization across empaneled public and private hospitals.

q: Which type of nursing leadership style involves staff nurses in decision-making, encourages shared governance, and improves team morale?
e: Democratic leadership engages team members collaboratively (best for unit morale and quality improvement), whereas Autocratic is reserved for rapid life-or-death emergencies like a Code Blue.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty (under which Right to Health is recognized)?
e: Article 21 guarantees Right to Life and Personal Liberty, which the Supreme Court of India has consistently interpreted to include the Right to Health and emergency medical care.

q: Convert 0.25 grams of a drug into milligrams (mg):
e: 1 gram = 1,000 mg; therefore 0.25 g × 1,000 = 250 mg.

q: A nurse walks 4 km North from the hospital, then turns right and walks 3 km East. What is the shortest straight-line distance back to the hospital?
e: By Pythagoras theorem: sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(16 + 9) = sqrt(25) = 5 km.

q: Which vitamin is essential for hepatic synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X?
e: Vitamin K (given as 1 mg IM to term newborns at birth) is required for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] In a mass-casualty train accident using START triage, a 32-year-old victim is not breathing initially, but resumes spontaneous respirations at 26/min after a simple jaw-thrust maneuver. Which triage color tag must the nurse assign?
e: Under START triage, if an apneic victim starts breathing after airway repositioning, they are tagged RED (Immediate). Only victims who remain apneic AFTER airway opening are tagged Black.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient with severe burns from a closed-space house fire arrives with singed nasal hairs, carbonaceous sputum, hoarse voice, and inspiratory stridor. What is the nurse's #1 priority?
o: Prepare for immediate endotracheal intubation and 100% humidified oxygen before airway edema closes the glottis
Calculate urine output over the next 4 hours
Insert a urinary catheter before assessing breathing
e: Singed nasal hairs, soot in sputum, hoarseness, and stridor signal thermal inhalation injury. Progressive airway edema can rapidly occlude the trachea—early prophylactic intubation is the top ABC priority.

q: [Mains Calculation] Dopamine is supplied as 400 mg in 250 mL D5W (1,600 mcg/mL). The physician orders Dopamine at 5 mcg/kg/min for an 80 kg patient in cardiogenic shock. What infusion pump rate (mL/hr) should the nurse set?
e: Dose/min = 5 × 80 = 400 mcg/min. Dose/hr = 400 × 60 = 24,000 mcg/hr. Concentration = 400,000 mcg / 250 mL = 1,600 mcg/mL. Rate = 24,000 / 1,600 = 15 mL/hr.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] Within the first hour of recognizing Septic Shock in the ICU (BP 78/42, lactate 4.6 mmol/L, fever 39.4°C), which sequence reflects the Surviving Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle?
o: Give antibiotics first, then draw blood cultures 6 hours later
Measure lactate, obtain blood cultures BEFORE broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, infuse 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, and start vasopressors (Norepinephrine) if MAP <65 mmHg
Wait for culture sensitivity results before starting any antibiotics
e: Surviving Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle: (1) Measure lactate, (2) Obtain blood cultures prior to antibiotics (without delaying antibiotics >45 min), (3) Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, (4) Rapid 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension/lactate >=4, (5) Vasopressors (Norepinephrine first-line) to keep MAP >=65 mmHg.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] Near the end of a patient's very first hemodialysis session for severe uremia (BUN 140 mg/dL), the patient develops severe headache, nausea, restlessness, and focal seizures. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
e: Rapid urea removal from blood during initial hemodialysis creates an osmotic gradient pulling water into brain cells, causing cerebral edema (Dialysis Disequilibrium Syndrome). Slow/stop dialysis and notify the nephrologist.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] Four ICU patients need attention simultaneously. Which patient should the charge nurse assess FIRST?
o: A stable post-op appendectomy patient requesting pain medication (pain 6/10)
A patient with Guillain-Barre Syndrome whose forced vital capacity dropped sharply and who has a weak cough and new dysphagia
A patient with chronic heart failure needing discharge teaching
A diabetic patient with a morning blood glucose of 198 mg/dL
e: Ascending paralysis in Guillain-Barre Syndrome threatens the diaphragm and airway (ABC priority); declining vital capacity and weak cough/dysphagia warn of imminent respiratory arrest requiring immediate airway assessment.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient with a C5 spinal cord injury suddenly develops throbbing headache, BP 214/118 mmHg, profuse sweating above the nipple line, and bradycardia (HR 48). What is the nurse's FIRST action?
o: Sit the patient upright (high-Fowler's), loosen tight clothing, and check for a kinked Foley catheter or fecal impaction (Autonomic Dysreflexia)
e: Autonomic dysreflexia (in injuries at/above T6) is a hypertensive emergency triggered by noxious stimuli below the lesion—most commonly a distended bladder or impacted bowel. Immediately elevate the head of bed to lower BP, then locate and remove the trigger.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] During an IV infusion of Doxorubicin (a vesicant chemotherapy agent), the patient complains of sudden burning pain at the peripheral IV site and blood return is absent. What is the FIRST nursing action?
o: Flush the IV cannula vigorously with 20 mL normal saline
Stop the chemotherapy infusion immediately while leaving the cannula in place to aspirate residual drug, notify oncology, and apply the drug-specific antidote/compress protocol
Remove the IV cannula immediately and massage the area firmly
Slow the drip rate to half speed
e: For vesicant extravasation: STOP infusion immediately, DO NOT flush, keep cannula in briefly to gently aspirate drug from the tissue if protocol indicates, elevate extremity, and apply specific antidote (e.g., Dexrazoxane/cold compress for anthracyclines).

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A G2P1 woman in active labor has a sudden tearing abdominal pain, cessation of contractions, easily palpable fetal parts through the abdominal wall, maternal tachycardia/hypotension, and absent FHR. What obstetric emergency has occurred?
o: Uterine rupture (especially high risk in prior C-section / VBAC)
e: Sudden tearing pain, loss of fetal station, cessation of contractions, palpable fetal parts externally, and maternal hypovolemic shock indicate uterine rupture—prepare immediately for emergency laparotomy/cesarean and massive blood transfusion.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] Under the Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP), a term newborn is limp and apneic after birth. After 30 seconds of warming, drying, stimulation, and clearing the airway, the baby remains apneic with HR 72 bpm. What is the NEXT immediate step?
o: Initiate Positive Pressure Ventilation (PPV) with room air (21% O2) at 40–60 breaths/min and attach pulse oximeter
Wait another 2 minutes for spontaneous crying
e: NRP Golden Minute: if apneic/gasping or HR <100 bpm after initial steps, start PPV (21% O2 for >=35 wks) immediately! Chest compressions are only started if HR remains <60 bpm DESPITE 30 seconds of effective corrective PPV.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A trauma patient with chest injury has absent breath sounds on the left side, tracheal deviation to the right, distended neck veins, and BP 74/40 mmHg. What emergency bedside intervention is immediately life-saving?
o: Order a portable chest X-ray and wait 20 minutes
Assist with immediate needle thoracostomy decompression (tension pneumothorax) followed by chest tube insertion
Start a rapid IV dopamine infusion alone
Place the patient in Trendelenburg position
e: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis—NEVER delay decompression for an X-ray. Immediate needle decompression (5th ICS anterior/mid-axillary line or 2nd ICS mid-clavicular line) converts tension into simple pneumothorax, followed by ICD tube.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] An ICU patient receiving Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN) via a central line finishes the current bag, and the next TPN bag is delayed by 45 minutes from pharmacy. What should the nurse infuse in the interim?
o: 10% Dextrose in water (D10W) at the same rate to prevent severe rebound hypoglycemia
Clamp the central line completely until the new bag arrives
e: Abruptly stopping high-dextrose TPN causes severe rebound hypoglycemia due to high endogenous insulin levels; hang D10W temporarily until the new TPN bag arrives.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) on mechanical ventilation has persistent severe hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 < 100) despite high PEEP. Which evidence-based ICU positioning intervention improves oxygenation and survival?
o: Prone positioning (12–16 hours/day) with lung-protective low tidal volume ventilation (4–6 mL/kg PBW)
e: Prone positioning recruits collapsed dorsal alveoli and improves ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) matching in severe ARDS, combined with low tidal volume (4–6 mL/kg predicted body weight) ventilation.

q: [Mains Calculation] A physician orders 1,200 units/hr of Heparin IV. The pharmacy supplies a bag containing 25,000 units of Heparin in 500 mL of D5W. At what rate (mL/hr) should the nurse program the infusion pump?
e: Concentration = 25,000 units / 500 mL = 50 units/mL. Infusion rate = 1,200 units/hr / 50 units/mL = 24 mL/hr.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A post-myocardial infarction patient suddenly develops muffled heart sounds, jugular venous distension, and hypotension (BP 82/56 mmHg) with pulsus paradoxus. This triad (Beck's triad) indicates:
e: Beck's triad (Hypotension + Distended neck veins + Muffled heart sounds) is diagnostic of cardiac tamponade—prepare immediately for emergency ultrasound-guided pericardiocentesis.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] During a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) to evaluate readiness for extubation in an ICU patient, which finding requires ABORTING the weaning trial and resuming full ventilator support?
o: Respiratory rate 38/min, paradoxical abdominal breathing, diaphoresis, and HR jumping from 84 to 132 bpm
e: Tachypnea (>35/min), diaphoresis, tachycardia, accessory muscle fatigue, or SpO2 <90% indicate weaning failure—immediately return the patient to supportive ventilation before respiratory arrest occurs.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient taking Fluoxetine (SSRI) starts Linezolid for MRSA pneumonia and develops agitation, hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, diaphoresis, and fever (39.5°C). Which syndrome is most likely?
e: Linezolid has weak MAOI activity; combining it with an SSRI triggers Serotonin Syndrome, distinguished from NMS by neuromuscular hyperexcitability (hyperreflexia + clonus) rather than 'lead-pipe' rigidity.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A postpartum mother 18 hours after normal delivery has a fundus that is firm, 2 fingerbreadths above the umbilicus, and shifted to the right with increased lochia flow. What is the nurse's FIRST action?
o: Assist the mother to void (or catheterize if unable) to empty a distended bladder
Apply cold packs to the abdomen
e: A firm uterus displaced above the umbilicus and to the right indicates a full urinary bladder pushing the uterus out of midline and impairing involution; emptying the bladder restores midline position and stops excess bleeding.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A 6-month-old infant with Tetralogy of Fallot suddenly becomes intensely cyanotic, tachypneic, and agitated while crying (hypercyanotic 'Tet spell'). What is the nurse's FIRST bedside action?
o: Place the infant flat on their back with legs extended
Place the infant immediately in knee-chest position, calm the infant, and administer 100% blow-by oxygen
e: Knee-chest (squatting in older children) increases systemic vascular resistance, decreasing right-to-left shunting across the VSD and forcing more blood into the pulmonary artery; follow with O2 and ordered IV morphine/fluids.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient with an acute ST-elevation MI (STEMI) is prescribed sublingual Nitroglycerin for ongoing chest pain. Before giving the dose, which patient history item makes Nitroglycerin STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED?
o: Use of Sildenafil (Viagra) within the past 24 hours or systolic BP < 90 mmHg
e: Combining nitrates with PDE-5 inhibitors (Sildenafil/Tadalafil) causes profound, refractory, potentially fatal hypotension; also withhold nitrates in right ventricular MI or SBP <90 mmHg.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient refuses a recommended blood transfusion due to deeply held religious beliefs after the physician explains the life-threatening risks. The patient is fully alert, oriented, and legally competent. What is the nurse's ethical duty?
o: Administer the transfusion once the patient falls asleep
Respect the patient's autonomy, ensure informed refusal is documented, and explore bloodless medical alternatives with the care team
Ask the hospital security to restrain the patient
Ignore the refusal because beneficence overrides competent adult autonomy
e: A mentally competent adult has the legal and ethical right (Autonomy) to refuse any medical treatment, including life-saving blood transfusions, once fully informed of consequences.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] On a busy medical-surgical ward, which task is MOST appropriate for the Registered Nursing Officer to delegate to a trained Nursing Assistant / Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
o: Performing the initial admission assessment of a newly transferred chest pain patient
Measuring routine vital signs and recording intake/output for a stable postoperative Day 2 patient
Evaluating the effectiveness of IV morphine 15 minutes after administration
Teaching a newly diagnosed diabetic patient how to self-inject insulin
e: Nursing Officers NEVER delegate assessment, clinical evaluation, teaching, or unstable patient care ('EAT': Evaluate, Assess, Teach). Routine vitals and I/O on a stable patient are safely delegable.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] A patient with Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH) has serum sodium of 116 mEq/L and begins having generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Which IV solution is ordered cautiously in the ICU, and why must Na+ correction NOT exceed 8–10 mEq/L in 24 hours?
o: 3% Hypertonic Saline via infusion pump; over-rapid correction risks Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome (central pontine myelinolysis)
e: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia (<120 mEq/L with seizures) is treated with cautious 3% NaCl via pump; raising Na+ faster than 8–10 mEq/L per 24 hours can cause irreversible Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome.

q: [Mains Clinical Case] While preparing to vaccinate a 6-week-old infant at a PHC immunization clinic, the nurse notices the Pentavalent vial was accidentally frozen solid overnight. Which test confirms freeze damage?
o: WHO Shake Test (comparing sedimentation speed against an intentionally frozen control vial)
Shaking the vial for 3 seconds and checking foam
e: Freeze-sensitive adsorbed vaccines (Pentavalent, DPT, Td, HepB, IPV) lose potency if frozen. The WHO Shake Test compares settling rate against a known frozen control—if the test vial settles at the same or faster rate (with granular floccules), DISCARD it.

q: [Mains Calculation] A pediatric patient weighing 20 kg is prescribed IV Paracetamol at 15 mg/kg/dose. The available IV Paracetamol bottle contains 10 mg/mL (1 g in 100 mL). How many mL should the nurse infuse for ONE dose?
e: Required dose = 15 mg/kg × 20 kg = 300 mg. Volume = 300 mg / (10 mg/mL) = 30 mL infused over 15 minutes.

q: A patient on mechanical ventilation suddenly develops absent breath sounds on the right, tracheal shift to the left, peak airway pressure jumping from 24 to 48 cm H2O, and BP 72/44 mmHg. What is the IMMEDIATE bedside priority?
o: Assist with immediate needle decompression of the right pleural space (tension pneumothorax)
Increase PEEP from 5 to 12 cm H2O
Wait for a bedside portable chest X-ray
e: Sudden high peak pressures, unilateral absent breath sounds, contralateral tracheal shift, and obstructive shock indicate barotrauma-induced tension pneumothorax—decompress immediately without waiting for imaging.

q: Which ECG rhythm requires SYNCHRONIZED cardioversion (rather than unsynchronized defibrillation) in an unstable patient with a palpable pulse and hypotension (BP 76/48 mmHg)?
o: Unstable Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT) or Atrial Fibrillation with RVR
e: Synchronized cardioversion delivers energy on the R wave to avoid the vulnerable T-wave period (R-on-T phenomenon) in unstable tachyarrhythmias WITH a pulse (SVT, AFib, AFlutter, monomorphic VT with pulse).

q: An ECG strip in the ICU shows polymorphic ventricular tachycardia twisting around the isoelectric baseline (Torsades de Pointes) in a patient with a prolonged QT interval. Which IV medication is first-line?
o: IV Magnesium Sulfate 1–2 g over 5–20 minutes
e: Torsades de Pointes is specifically treated with IV Magnesium Sulfate (even if serum Mg2+ is normal) plus defibrillation if pulseless and discontinuing QT-prolonging drugs.

q: A patient with acute ischemic stroke arrives 2 hours after symptom onset. Before administering IV Alteplase (tPA), blood pressure MUST be lowered and maintained below which threshold?
e: AHA/ASA guidelines mandate BP <185/110 mmHg prior to IV thrombolysis and <180/105 mmHg for the first 24 hours after tPA to prevent fatal hemorrhagic transformation.

q: Interpret this ABG from a chronic COPD patient: pH 7.36, PaCO2 56 mmHg, HCO3- 31 mEq/L.
e: pH is back inside the normal range (7.35–7.45) on the acidic side (<7.40), PaCO2 is elevated (primary respiratory acidosis), and HCO3- is elevated (renal compensation) = fully compensated respiratory acidosis.

q: During hemodialysis, a patient suddenly reports severe chest tightness, dyspnea, and dizziness; the nurse notices air bubbles entering the venous return line. What is the FIRST step?
o: Clamp the venous blood line and stop the blood pump immediately, then place patient in left lateral Trendelenburg
Flush the line with 100 mL normal saline
Elevate the head of the bed to 90 degrees
e: Immediately stop the blood pump and clamp the venous return line to halt further air entry, position left lateral Trendelenburg (Durant's maneuver), give 100% O2, and alert the physician.

q: A patient with a tibial shaft fracture in a plaster cast reports excruciating pain unrelieved by IV morphine, pain on passive toe extension, and tingling in the foot. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?
o: Elevate the leg high above heart level and apply tight ice packs
Reassure the patient that cast pain peaks at 48 hours
Keep the limb at heart level, notify the orthopedic surgeon immediately for cast bivalving/fasciotomy (Compartment Syndrome)
Administer an extra oral NSAID and reassess in 2 hours
e: Severe out-of-proportion pain worsened by passive stretch and paresthesia are early hallmark signs of Acute Compartment Syndrome. Do NOT elevate above heart level or apply ice (worsens arterial perfusion); prepare immediately for cast splitting/fasciotomy.

q: Twenty-four hours after a closed femur fracture, a young adult develops acute tachypnea, hypoxemia (SpO2 85%), confusion, and petechial rash across the anterior chest, neck, and axillae. Which complication is suspected?
e: The classic triad of Fat Embolism Syndrome (24–72 hrs after long-bone fracture) is respiratory distress/hypoxemia, neurological confusion, and petechiae on the upper chest/axillae/conjunctiva.

q: A patient with a right-sided chest tube accidentally pulls the tube completely out of the chest wall during ambulation. What should the nurse do IMMEDIATELY?
o: Reinsert the dislodged chest tube back into the incision
Apply a sterile occlusive petroleum gauze dressing taped on THREE sides and notify the physician immediately
Leave the wound open to air
Tape a dry gauze tightly on all four sides immediately
e: A three-sided sterile occlusive dressing acts as a one-way flutter valve allowing trapped pleural air to escape on exhalation while preventing air entry on inhalation (preventing tension pneumothorax). Never reinsert a pulled chest tube.

q: During active labor, continuous CTG shows abrupt V-shaped FHR drops to 85 bpm with rapid recovery that vary in timing relative to contractions (Variable Decelerations). What is the underlying cause and FIRST nursing action?
o: Umbilical cord compression; reposition the mother (side-to-side or knee-chest) and check for cord prolapse
Fetal head compression; continue routine observation
e: VEAL CHOP: Variable decelerations = Cord compression. First action is maternal position change (left/right lateral or knee-chest) to relieve cord pressure, discontinue oxytocin if running, give O2, and check for occult/overt prolapse.

q: A primigravida at 35 weeks with preeclampsia develops RUQ abdominal pain, AST/ALT 4× normal, platelets 62,000/mm3, and hemolysis on peripheral smear. Which syndrome is present?
o: HELLP Syndrome (Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets)
e: HELLP syndrome is a life-threatening variant of severe preeclampsia requiring stabilization (BP control, MgSO4 seizure prophylaxis, blood products if needed) and prompt delivery.

q: Which three steps comprise Active Management of the Third Stage of Labor (AMTSL) recommended by WHO to prevent postpartum hemorrhage?
o: Routine episiotomy, fundal pressure, and early cord clamping
Manual removal of placenta in all deliveries, ergometrine, and vaginal packing
Delayed pushing, supine positioning, and ice packs
Administration of uterotonic (Oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV) immediately after birth, controlled cord traction, and uterine tone assessment/massage
e: AMTSL reduces PPH by >60%: (1) Prophylactic Oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV within 1 minute of birth (most critical step), (2) Controlled cord traction with counter-traction, and (3) Post-delivery uterine tone assessment/massage.

q: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks in preterm labor is ordered two doses of Betamethasone 12 mg IM 24 hours apart. What is the primary purpose of this therapy?
o: To accelerate fetal pulmonary surfactant production and reduce neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
e: Antenatal corticosteroids (Betamethasone 12 mg IM q24h × 2 or Dexamethasone 6 mg IM q12h × 4) between 24 and 34 weeks stimulate type II pneumocytes to produce surfactant, reducing RDS and IVH.

q: After suction evacuation of a complete Hydatidiform Mole (molar pregnancy), what is the MOST essential follow-up instruction for the woman over the next 6–12 months?
o: Avoid pregnancy using reliable contraception and undergo serial serum beta-hCG monitoring to detect gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (choriocarcinoma)
Attempt conception immediately to normalize hormones
Stop all follow-up once vaginal bleeding ends
e: Rising or plateauing beta-hCG indicates persistent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia/choriocarcinoma; reliable contraception prevents a new pregnancy from masking rising hCG levels.

q: A 5-week-old male infant presents with forceful, projectile non-bilious vomiting immediately after feeds, visible gastric peristalsis, and a palpable olive-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant. Which acid-base disturbance is classic?
e: Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis causes persistent loss of gastric HCl and K+, producing hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis—correct fluid/electrolytes BEFORE Ramstedt pyloromyotomy.

q: An 8-month-old infant presents with sudden paroxysms of severe inconsolable crying drawing knees to the abdomen, alternating with lethargy, and passes dark red 'currant jelly' stools. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e: Telescoping of one bowel segment into another (typically ileocolic intussusception) causes episodic colicky pain, sausage-shaped RUQ mass, and bloody mucus 'currant jelly' stools; pneumatic/hydrostatic enema is diagnostic and therapeutic.

q: A 3-year-old child is admitted with a firm, smooth, unilateral abdominal mass suspected to be Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma). Which sign MUST the nurse place over the child's crib?
o: 'Keep child flat on back at all times'
e: Palpating a Wilms tumor risks rupturing the fragile tumor capsule and seeding malignant cells throughout the peritoneal cavity.

q: A 2-year-old child with a harsh 'barking' seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor at rest, and 'steeple sign' on neck X-ray is diagnosed with acute laryngotracheobronchitis (Croup). Which two medications are standard first-line treatment?
o: Oral Dexamethasone and nebulized Racemic Epinephrine
e: Systemic corticosteroids (Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg) reduce subglottic airway edema, and nebulized Epinephrine rapidly relieves stridor at rest (observe >=2–4 hours post-epi for rebound stridor).

q: A patient is brought to the ER after accidental organophosphate insecticide ingestion with pinpoint pupils, profuse salivation, bronchorrhea, bradycardia, and muscle fasciculations. Which antidote pair is indicated?
e: Organophosphates inhibit acetylcholinesterase ('DUMBELS' cholinergic crisis). High-dose IV Atropine dries life-threatening bronchorrhea/reverses bradycardia, while Pralidoxime (2-PAM) reactivates phosphorylated AChE to reverse nicotinic muscle paralysis.

q: When administering concentrated Potassium Chloride (KCl) intravenously to a patient with serum K+ 2.7 mEq/L, which nursing safety rule is ABSOLUTE?
o: Give KCl as a rapid IV bolus over 1 minute for faster correction
NEVER administer IV push/undiluted; dilute in IV fluid and infuse via pump (max 10 mEq/hr peripherally) only after confirming adequate urine output
Mix KCl directly into packed RBC units
Administer IM into the deltoid muscle
e: Undiluted IV push KCl causes instant lethal cardiac arrest. Always dilute, use an infusion pump (peripheral max 10 mEq/hr; central line up to 20 mEq/hr with cardiac monitor), and verify urine output >=30 mL/hr.

q: Which anti-tubercular drug in the first-line HRZE regimen is classically associated with retrobulbar optic neuritis (loss of red-green color vision and decreased visual acuity)?
e: Remember 'E for Eye': Ethambutol causes dose-dependent optic neuritis (test baseline and monthly visual acuity/Ishihara color plates). Rifampicin causes orange-red urine; Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia/gout; Isoniazid causes peripheral neuropathy.

q: To verify safe serum levels and prevent nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity in a patient receiving IV Gentamicin every 8 hours, when should the nurse draw a TROUGH blood sample?
o: Immediately BEFORE (within 30 minutes prior to) the next scheduled dose
At midnight regardless of dosing time
e: Trough levels reflect drug clearance and toxicity risk—draw right before the next dose (usually before the 3rd or 4th dose). Peak levels are drawn 30 minutes after IV infusion completes.

q: Which evidence-based care bundle measure MOST effectively reduces Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP) in mechanically ventilated ICU patients?
o: Keeping the patient completely flat at 0 degrees
Changing ventilator circuits every 4 hours routinely
Elevating head of bed to 30°–45°, daily sedation vacation/extubation readiness assessment, and oral care with Chlorhexidine
Routine instillation of normal saline before every suction pass
e: IHI VAP Bundle: HOB elevation 30°–45°, daily sedation interruption & SBT assessment, peptic ulcer & DVT prophylaxis, and daily oral chlorhexidine hygiene. Never instill routine saline before suctioning.

q: A nursing officer sustains a deep needle-stick injury while drawing blood from an HIV-positive patient. What is the immediate local wound action and ideal window to start HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)?
o: Squeeze the finger vigorously to bleed out the virus and start PEP within 10 days
Wash gently with soap and running water (do NOT squeeze/scrub), report immediately, and start 28-day PEP ideally within 2 hours (max 72 hours)
Soak in undiluted bleach and wait for 6-week ELISA result
Apply hydrogen peroxide and skip PEP if wearing single gloves
e: NACO/CDC PEP protocol: Wash immediately with soap & water without squeezing/bleach, report to occupational health, and start 3-drug antiretroviral PEP ASAP (ideally <2 hrs, never beyond 72 hrs) for 28 days.

q: When flushing a Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter (PICC) or central venous line, what is the MINIMUM syringe size that should be used to prevent catheter rupture from excessive pressure?
e: Smaller-barrel syringes generate dangerously high PSI pressure that can rupture a PICC/CVC catheter. Always use a 10 mL (or larger) syringe with pulsatile push-pause flushing.

q: Which blood type is the Universal Donor for Packed Red Blood Cells (PRBCs) and Universal Donor for Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) respectively?
